set.body:
Defect: Reading a workbook at all. Three hazards, all measured on the real Friends bytes.

Do: corpus-intake/Xlsx.scala -- zip entry, shared strings, sheet rows as Raw cells, JDK StAX (no new dependency; ADR line). The declared <dimension> is NOT trusted.

Tests: Synthetic workbooks ONLY -- no corpus bytes enter Git (design contract rule 14(d)). Reproduce: a sheet whose declared dimension exceeds its data (measured: friendsSRMStoryBoard declares A1:O58 and holds 14 data rows -- this is exactly how the intake manifest came to claim 57 events from the WRONG EPISODE); a header-only sheet with zero data rows (measured: all 57 Friends eventseg CSVs are 63 bytes, header only); trailing padding past content (measured: six Friends sheets pre-filled to SecondsOfRecall 3000).

Mutants (SD1 — each must die, recorded by name): trust the declared dimension -> dimension test fails. Treat a header-only sheet as success -> empty-CSV test fails. Trim on the seconds column rather than content columns C-I -> padding test fails.

Exit: The three intake-manifest errors caused by these hazards are each caught by a regression test.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-17-annotation-intake-contract.md S3, P2a
set.title: intake P2a: xlsx reader via JDK StAX, declared dimension not trusted
